scams.name: Airport Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: You land at Split Airport and head to the taxi rank, where a driver approaches immediately offering a ride to town. He quotes what sounds like a reasonable price, but the journey costs you €80 when the official rate is around €30-35. No meter is running and he insisted on a verbal agreement. Split Airport taxis have a documented reputation for overcharging tourists who don't know the going rate.
scams.avoidance: Take the official Croatia Airlines shuttle bus to the city center — cheap and reliable Use Uber, which operates in Split, for transparent pricing Only use taxis from the official rank and insist on the meter or fixed rate confirmation
scams.location: Split Airport to the city center

scams.name: Diocletian's Palace Unofficial Guide
scams.description: You enter the ancient Diocletian's Palace through the Golden Gate and are immediately approached by a friendly man who offers to show you 'secret' underground passages and Roman engineering that normal tourists miss. He walks with you for 45 minutes pointing out architectural details, and at the end presents a bill of €40-50 per person. There was no price agreement, and he insists this is the standard rate.
scams.avoidance: Book guided tours through the official Split tourist office on Peristyle Hire guides only through your hotel or accredited agencies with visible credentials Agree on price in writing before starting any tour
scams.location: Peristyle square and Golden Gate, Diocletian's Palace

scams.name: Riva Promenade Restaurant Overcharge
scams.description: You sit down at one of the gorgeous terrace restaurants on the Riva with views of the harbor and order a simple seafood dish. When the bill arrives, there's a 'service charge,' a 'terrace fee,' and a 'cover charge' that weren't on the menu — the total is nearly double what you expected. Some restaurants also add each small piece of bread to the bill as a separate charge.
scams.avoidance: Ask specifically if there is a cover charge or terrace fee before sitting Decline bread if you don't want it — in Croatia it's often charged separately Check the menu carefully for * footnotes about additional charges
scams.location: Restaurants along the Riva waterfront promenade

scams.name: Nightclub 'Gentlemen's Club' Trap
scams.description: After a night out, you follow a friendly local who suggests a 'great bar' nearby. Inside you're seated and attractive staff immediately order drinks on your behalf. At the end of the night the bill is astronomically inflated — €50 per drink, €500 minimum covers — and large bouncers prevent you from leaving until you pay. Some tourists have been forced to ATM withdrawals under escort.
scams.avoidance: Never follow strangers to bars they recommend aggressively Ask for a written menu and prices before ordering anything in an unfamiliar venue Stick to well-reviewed bars on Google Maps with lots of tourist reviews
scams.location: Old Town evening bar and club areas

scams.name: Island Ferry Ticket Tout
scams.description: You want to take a ferry to Hvar or Brač and ask around for tickets near the port. A man approaches saying the official booth queue is very long and he can sell you tickets now. You pay him and get what looks like a valid ticket. At the gate, your ticket scans as invalid and the touts have already disappeared into the crowd.
scams.avoidance: Buy ferry tickets only from the official Jadrolinija counter at the terminal Book Jadrolinija tickets in advance online at jadrolinija.hr No legitimate ticket seller approaches you in the street or parking area
scams.location: Split ferry terminal, near Jadrolinija dock

scams.name: Pickpockets in Old Town Crowds
scams.description: You're squeezing through the impossibly narrow medieval alleys of Diocletian's Palace in July, shoulder to shoulder with hundreds of other tourists. The crush of bodies makes it natural for hands to brush against you, and in that anonymity a skilled pickpocket extracts your phone from a back pocket. You don't notice until you stop for a coffee twenty minutes later.
scams.avoidance: Never keep anything in back pockets inside the Old Town in summer Use a crossbody anti-theft bag or money belt Visit the most crowded parts of the Old Town early morning or late evening
scams.location: Narrow streets of Diocletian's Palace during peak season
